title: People love pointing at Sarah for laughing.
paragraphs: People love pointing at Sarah for laughing.
But they missed Abraham.

In Genesis 17:17, the Bible says:
“Then Abraham fell on his face and laughed and said to himself, ‘Shall a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? Shall Sarah, who is ninety years old, bear a child?’”
Read that again.
Abraham laughed too.

Not because God was weak.
But because the promise sounded impossible to human ears.
And that is exactly how God works.

He speaks into dead places.
He promises life where the body says no.
He declares a future that human logic cannot produce.
That moment exposes something in all of us.
We say we believe God, but when His promise collides with our limitations, our hearts often laugh before they trust.

That is why this story is not ultimately about Abraham’s strength.
It is about God’s faithfulness.

Romans 4:19–21 says Abraham, “He did not weaken in faith when he considered his own body, which was as good as dead… No unbelief made him waver concerning the promise of God, but he grew strong in his faith… fully convinced that God was able to do what he had promised.”
So yes, Abraham laughed.
But his laughter was not the end of the story.

God stayed.
God spoke.
God fulfilled what He said.
And that points to something even greater.
Because the real impossible promise was never just Isaac.
It was salvation for sinners through Jesus Christ.

We were spiritually dead.
We could not save ourselves.
We could not produce righteousness from our own brokenness.
But God made a promise.
Romans 5:8 says, “but God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
And Ephesians 2:8–9 says, “For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God, not a result of works, so that no one may boast.”
That means this:
The same God who brought Isaac out of impossibility brings new life out of dead sinners through Jesus.

So don’t read Genesis 17 like it is a story about flawless faith.
It is a story about a flawless God.
And maybe that is the part people missed.

You laughed.
You doubted.
You struggled.
But God’s mercy did not collapse under your weakness.
Still, do not stay in unbelief.

Repent.
Turn from self-reliance.
Trust the One who keeps every word.
Trust Jesus Christ, the true Son of promise, who died for sin and rose again so broken people could be redeemed.
If this found you, it’s not by accident.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
